From 16de4c6a8fe9ff497ca1aba33ef0dbee09f11952 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Bartosz Golaszewski <bartosz.golaszewski@oss.qualcomm.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Dec 2025 10:44:12 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] reset: gpio: suppress bind attributes in sysfs

This is a special device that's created dynamically and is supposed to
stay in memory forever. We also currently don't have a devlink between
it and the actual reset consumer. Suppress sysfs bind attributes so that
user-space can't unbind the device because - as of now - it will cause a
use-after-free splat from any user that puts the reset control handle.

Fixes: cee544a40e44 ("reset: gpio: Add GPIO-based reset controller")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Bartosz Golaszewski <bartosz.golaszewski@oss.qualcomm.com>
Reviewed-by: Krzysztof Kozlowski <krzysztof.kozlowski@oss.qualcomm.com>
Signed-off-by: Philipp Zabel <p.zabel@pengutronix.de>

diff --git a/drivers/reset/reset-gpio.c b/drivers/reset/reset-gpio.c
index e5512b3b596b..626c4c639c15 100644
--- a/drivers/reset/reset-gpio.c
+++ b/drivers/reset/reset-gpio.c
@@ -111,6 +111,7 @@ static struct auxiliary_driver reset_gpio_driver = {
 	.id_table	= reset_gpio_ids,
 	.driver	= {
 		.name = "reset-gpio",
+		.suppress_bind_attrs = true,
 	},
 };
 module_auxiliary_driver(reset_gpio_driver);
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file, `drivers/reset/reset-gpio.c`, by adding `suppress_bind_attrs = true` to the driver structure's `.driver` field.

This change suppresses the sysfs bind/unbind attributes for the driver, preventing user-space from unbinding the dynamically-created reset GPIO device. Without this suppression, an unbind operation could cause a use-after-free vulnerability because the device lacks a devlink with its consumer. The fix directly addresses the bug introduced by commit cee544a40e44.

This is a special device that's created dynamically and is supposed to

user-space can't unbind the device because - as of now - it will cause a

Fixes: cee544a40e44 ("reset: gpio: Add GPIO-based reset controller")

Here is the root cause:
The reset-gpio driver creates a device dynamically that is intended to stay in memory forever, but lacks a devlink with the actual reset consumer. Without suppressing bind attributes in sysfs, user-space can unbind the device, leading to a use-after-free vulnerability because the device can be removed while still being referenced.

Here is the patch:

 		.name = "reset-gpio",
+		.suppress_bind_attrs = true,

 };

Root cause:
The reset-gpio driver creates a device dynamically that is intended to stay in memory forever, but lacks a devlink with the actual reset consumer. Without suppressing bind attributes in sysfs, user-space can unbind the device, leading to a use-after-free vulnerability because the device can be removed while still being referenced.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
	.driver	= {
		.name = "reset-gpio",
	},
Reason:
The driver definition does not set `.suppress_bind_attrs = true`, allowing user-space to unbind the device through sysfs. Since the reset-gpio device is dynamically created with the intention of staying in memory forever and lacks a devlink to its consumer, unbinding it causes a use-after-free when any user puts the reset control handle.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
	.driver	= {
		.name = "reset-gpio",
+		.suppress_bind_attrs = true,
	},
Reason:
Setting `.suppress_bind_attrs = true` prevents sysfs bind/unbind attributes from being created for this device, so user-space cannot trigger a removal. This ensures the device remains in memory, eliminating the use-after-free vulnerability.

The fix requires adding that attribute. Since the snippet lacks it, the bug is present.
